Hi Andre,

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed set of next steps so we can qualify the right deployment mode for Legacy Bank (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private on-prem air-gapped):

- Summary: You confirmed the primary requirement is an on-prem, air-gapped deployment for model inference tied to regulated customer data. Secondary priorities are predictable throughput for peak batch scoring and strict key management controls.
- Open/ask items we promised to follow up on:

  2) Offline upgrade and patching process (how images/artifacts are delivered to an air-gapped cluster).
  3) Network footprint for offline ops and any NFS/SAN requirements.
  4) KMS/HSM integration details and whether you require an HSM-backed key store.

Attached are a first-pass hardware matrix and an SOW draft to help frame options (redwood_onprem_hardware_matrix.pdf, sow_draft_v1.pdf).

Proposed next steps:
- 30-min SE deep-dive to walk hardware matrix and offline upgrade flow (I suggest Thursday 5/17 or Friday 5/18).
- Procurement stopgap: we'll circulate rough T&&C items for review.

Can you confirm the best contact for procurement and whether the team has an existing HSM vendor? Also, are there any hard constraints on rack U height or power/cooling per rack?

Thanks — I’ll loop Dylan for the SE call scheduling and he can answer the hardware/ops questions in detail.

Andre,

Quick answers and next actions — I've included Dylan to provide the technical write-up and we attached an updated hardware matrix with options for minimal and scaled configs. See the attached redwood_onprem_hardware_matrix.pdf.

High-level responses: 
- Air-gap/upgrade: We support fully air-gapped deployments. We provide a signed, versioned release bundle (tarball) that can be delivered via USB, private S3 transfer, or on-prem transfer mechanism. No outbound connection is required for runtime or updates.
- KMS/HSM: We integrate with on-prem HSMs (Thales, Gemalto) using our on-prem KMS connector; HSM-backed keys are supported. We'll need a cross-team call to exchange certs and network details for the KMS connector.
- Storage/KV cache: NVMe is recommended for KV cache performance; for a single rack minimal config we recommend 4x high-memory GPUs with 2TB NVMe per node as a starting point (Dylan will share more specifics).
- Upgrade/rollback: We deliver upgrade bundles plus a documented rollback procedure. In air-gapped mode, rollback is performed by applying the prior signed bundle and restarting services under a controlled maintenance window; we'll advise a staged canary inside your lab subnet before cluster-wide rollout.

Attached are the hardware matrix and a draft SOW for procurement. Next: Dylan, can you enumerate the minimal and scaled GPU configs and the offline upgrade checklist we should share with Legacy Ops?

Thanks,
Marissa

Andre / team,

Following up with the technical details we discussed. See the network_diagram_stubs.txt attached for an example offline transfer topology. High-level recommendations and answers below:

Recommended baseline (single-rack, initial prod):
- Nodes: 3 inference nodes + 1 control/management node.
- GPUs per inference node: 2 x NVIDIA A100 80GB (or H100 equivalent if available) — good balance for throughput and memory for medium-size models.
- CPU: Dual 24-core per node for inference driver and pre/post processing.
- RAM: 768GB per inference node recommended for larger KV caches.
- Storage: 4TB NVMe per inference node for KV cache and model artifacts; separate 8TB for logs/retention on the management node (these can be mounted on SAN if preferred).
- Network: 100GbE leaf-to-leaf with a private management VLAN. For offline artifact staging, we recommend an isolated transfer jump host with dual NICs and direct-attached storage (USB/SATA racks) for import.

Scaled (multi-rack) guidance:
- Add inference nodes in multiples of 3 to maintain redundancy; provide additional GPUs per node if you need higher concurrency.
- We support horizontal scaling with autoscaling policies controlled by the Redwood control plane (no external outbound).

Air-gap upgrade process (offline ops):
1) Redwood prepares a signed release bundle (sha256 + signature) and verifies checksum on your import host.
2) Transfer method: USB -> jump host -> internal artifact repo OR private S3 transfer via air-gapped gateway your team controls.
3) Staging: apply bundle to a single canary node in your lab VLAN and run acceptance tests (we provide a test harness).
4) Rollout: sequential apply across nodes with health checks; rollback is applying previous bundle as needed.
5) Support: we provide an upgrade runbook and a 4-hour initial guidance window during your first production upgrade; extended SRE engagement available as paid add-on.

Other notes:
- HSM/KMS: we support Thales HSM over PKCS#11 and can validate key wrapping locally. We'll need to exchange network/IP allowlists for the KMS connector.
- Acceptance testing: plan for a 3-5 day Redwood acceptance window once hardware is on-site for smoke tests and throughput benchmarking.
